---
title: "Gaussianization — Labs"
---

Six hands-on notebooks in two tracks, mirroring the
[dependence labs](../../dependence/labs/index.qmd).  The verb is **simplify**:
build the invertible map, run it forward to measure and backward to generate.

## Learn-the-Tool Track

| Lab | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| [Tool 1 — The 1-D transform](lab-tool1-change-of-variables.qmd) | rank → Gaussian; invertibility by hand |
| [Tool 2 — RBIG forward & backward](lab-tool2-rbig.qmd) | marginal + rotation, iterated; sampling |
| [Tool 3 — MI by Gaussianization](lab-tool3-mutual-information.qmd) | estimate mutual information; validate it |

## Do-the-Job Track

| Lab | Deliverable |
|-----|-------------|
| [Job A — Validate the estimator](lab-jobA-validate.qmd) | calibration vs the Gaussian closed form |
| [Job B — Gaussianize the basket](lab-jobB-gaussianize-basket.qmd) | normal-scores + pairwise MI on real returns |
| [Job C — Generate scenarios](lab-jobC-scenarios.qmd) | RBIG backward to sample joint return scenarios |

## Shared Setup

```python
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd() / "src"))
from lectures import plotting, datasets
from lectures.gaussianization import gaussianize_1d
from rbig import AnnealedRBIG
from lectures.measures import mutual_information_xy, cocrash_fraction
plotting.set_style("notes")
```

The do-the-job labs load real returns with `datasets.load_returns()`.
